title: good for neurodivergent people especially
body: This app has a great design for people who can't handle too much busyness. It also has a critical function, which means the reminder nags you until you check it off., which is great for taking medications. You can set repeat times and amounts, duplicate reminders, choose from different non-offensive reminder sounds, turn on a critical alert (sound comes through even if phone is muted or on Do Not Disturb), and sync with icloud. I think it's good for people who want a simple but effective way to be reminded. Plus it has timers that you can customize (e.g., coffee steeping for 4 minutes). This is useful because I forget to take out teabags all the time.

title: As lazy an app as I feel
body:
It’s bad. Don’t bother.

Literally every single app on the market is better than this. It’s the Notes app you have on your phone, but harder to use, as you have to tap a bunch to get a due time set. No easy reorganising, no categorising by work or home or chore etc easily, no auto schedule, no relevant or decent integration... the list goes on, but my list won’t be in Due.

I’d rate it 1 star if it was free; it’s something you’d expect a uni student to make for free to bolster their portfolio with their first app. Because it’s paid, I have to write that it’s less than 0 stars.

Even better, they ask you to subscribe for their “yearly” new features. Get this - besides some recent MASSIVE updates this year (wait for it...... widgets...! Yes, I was being sarcastic), they’ve only actually delivered updates for one year out of the past half decade. So not only is this the crappiest most featureless app I’ve ever downloaded, it’s also the worst I’ve ever paid for. And I have to wait forever to request a refund.

So save yourself the effort I now have to go through.

title: When you really can't forget something
body:

Recurring, nagging reminders are terrific. For example, every month, it reminds me to pay rent. The alarm goes off, I'm not at a computer. I snooze it for an hour. It goes off again. I pay my rent, hit the "done" button, and the same task cycles forward a month.

Simple but brilliantly effective. So useful, it's on my home screen. Get it.

title: Frustrating
body: I bought the App and Desktop version to sync across 3 devices - iPad, iPhone and iMac - using iCloud.  In fact, I've found the iPhone and iPad repeatedly 'time out' when syncing.  Only a hard reset of the mobile device seems to trigger a satisfactory sync - inconvenient and frustrating.  It's pointless having it on iPad and iPhone because switching off the reminder alarm on one device, doesn't switch off the other, unless the second device is on with Due actually running.  Developer advice on the website suggests turning off the snooze/repeat reminder on the iPad, but that seems to defeat the purpose.  In any case the snooze feature on mobile devices can only be set to 1 minute or 1 hour - not necessarily practical.  In the end, Due isn't as user-friendly as the native iOS App 'Reminders' which comes with iPad and iPhone and which seamlessly syncs via iCal on a Mac.  If Reminders isn't good enough for you, try BusyToDo which is much more intuitive and allows for reminder categories, such as 'work', 'home' etc.

title: Avoid this if you need recurring reminders
body:
The UI design is pretty good, as others have observed. But there is one crazy shortcoming with recurring alarms that makes me regret buying this app:

Once you have set up a recurring reminder and it has 'fired', you have to go into the app and press the individual reminder's "Repeat" button - if not, the app treats it as complete and you will never hear from it again, regardless of how you set it up. I thought I must have misunderstood this because it is such a strange requirement, but the developer confirmed it (to his credit, he responded quickly).

Not even Apple's built-in reminder app does this, so it appears to be an arbitrary design choice -  and a really strange and unnecessary one.

Save your money and get "Alarmed" instead - its reminder functionality is better, it does more, its powerful basic version is free and the in-app upgrade is cheaper than Due.

title: Simply great!
body:
Twenty-odd years ago there was a simple but powerful reminder application for the Mac called Smart Alarms. One its best features was the ease of 'snoozing' an alarm, yet it would continue to nag you so that an event was not overlooked. How I've longed for a replacement - and at last I've found it!

'Due' is the easiest reminder app that I have used, and I've tried (and paid for) many. I still use a fully fledged organiser app but for quick reminders, 'Due' is simply close to perfect.

I can't believe that there are negative reviews - to each his own I guess.

title: Excelente, maaaas...
body:
O app é bom demais, faz tudo que eu preciso.
Cada lembrete pode ser personalizado de uma forma diferente, tendo várias opções de som, de repetição (semanal, anual, todo 1º dia útil do mês, etc.) e de insistência (lembrar a cada x minutos até que eu conclua ou adie) que não te permitem esquecer de nada.
Ele não tem a opção de lembrete por localização, apenas por horário (não é um problema pra mim, mas pode ser relevante para outros).
Retirei 2 estrelas por conta de 2 motivos (se forem alterados eu as acrescento): 
1) de vez em quando percebo que não tocou nenhum lembrete no dia, e quando abro o app tem dezenas de lembretes atrasados e nada de notificação. Esqueci de mandar um e-mail importante... Isso precisa ser corrigido, pois as notificações são a alma do app! 
2) acho um abuso pagar um valor alto no app e não ter acesso às novidades futuras. É preciso assinar um pacote anual para ter acesso a novas funções. O app funciona bem com o que tem, valeu cada centavo e a empresa tem o direito de fazer isso, mas se vier um app concorrente que não tenha essa limitação, dou tchau no mesmo dia...

Isto ocorre em um outro aplicativo que utilizo chamado ERRANDS, mas como ele vem apresentando muitos problemas de sincronização, optei por este que venho a comentar.

Além disso, a criação de um campo tipo NOTAS, para adição de mais detalhes para o compromisso agendado!!!

Aguardo resposta e mais uma vez parabéns!!!

title: It’s better than the built in iPhone reminder app
body:
I do like this app and as title says, it’s better than the built in iPhone reminder app. I like and hate how it keeps reminding me to do the thing but I do end up doing the thing which is my ultimate goal. 

What I find this app is missing and why I didn’t give it five stars is how it doesn’t provide you with an option to remind yourself 15min before the event. If there was an option to select drive or travel time - I feel it would help so many to plan for how long it takes to get to your appointment. Right now I have to include the time the appointment is in the title and set the timer for approx 30 min down to 15 minutes depending on the distance and weather. 

I would also like to be able to select some reminders to not be able to push to my smart watch. If say medication reminders can be pushed but the minor less urgent reminds don’t and just appear on my phone. That would be lovely.

Thanks!

author: Jonathan Bussières

title: The Best
body:
I don’t normally write reviews for app but this one is an exception. Due is exactly what I needed. A fast and easy to use reminder app. I don’t need anything complicated like different folders or sections. I just need a list of reminders and I need the app to work perfectly on my phone,ipad and most importantly my Apple Watch that will remind me when it matters.

Due check all those boxes. My favorite feature is that the smart language is extremely powerfull while supporting multiple languages (I can write ‘tomorrow’ or ‘demain’ which is french for tomorrow and both will work) and it takes me only a mere second to create a new reminder. 

I can also snooze or report a reminder easily with the little menu either from notification or on my phone or Apple Watch.

If you run your life with reminders like me then Due is a most have. Give it a try and stick with it for a couple of days and you’ll never go back to your old app or workflow.

title: My most used reminder app
body:
Due is there for those things that you have to deal with immediately. I won’t claim that it’s the only reminder app that you need, but I find it to be my most used one. 
I use the app in two ways: 
1) either for things (either important or frivolous) that I need to do on another app or remember later, but I don’t want to do immediately because I’m with family, in a meeting etc. 
2) things that I just cannot put off.
The relentless reminders are invaluable to me, and anyone who can’t afford to miss a reminder. I don’t always check my to-do lists on other apps, but due makes it impossible for me to procrastinate the tasks that I set on it. Even if I miss the first notification, it will eventually get my attention  
There is no other reminder app that has less frills, and Due allows me to input reminders faster than any other app that I’ve tried. The quick time selections allow me to be reminded at times that I’m likely to have the time to deal with it.
I’m looking forward to trying version 3, and will always pay for the new version of this app, especially considering the low price point and the amount of use that I get from it. 
Kudos to the developer for keeping it around for as long as it has been, and for resisting the urge to turn it into a bulky program.

title: Great new update, but a couple of bugs
body:
This app was already the best reminder app I have ever found, but now it has been even further improved. I will never look for another reminders app again. 

However, do not use the "sync to Dropbox" feature. It causes the app to freeze and crash a lot when it is enabled. After realizing this I tried turning off all syncing options, but this didn't stop it from syncing. I actually had to unlink it from my Dropbox account to restore the non-crashy performance.

Another thing, be careful when swiping left to mark a reminder as completed. If you swipe too far, you will delete it instead. That is easy to do. This will only be a problem if you are marking a REPEATING item however, as it will prevent all future occurrences of the reminder when you delete it. Otherwise I imagine most people probably wouldn't care if they delete an item or just mark it as done. If you do delete it, there is a handy red "undo delete" bar that appears at the bottom of the screen briefly. And if you realize your error after this bar has vanished, "shake to undo" will still undo the delete if you have not done anything since. Of course when you swipe left on an item, it happens so fast you might not realize you have deleted something instead of only marking it as done. This is something to pay close attention to.

Other than these issues, it is a wonderful app and I love the new update. It is much more customizable than before. And the 45 new notification sounds that have been added are really cool sounds!! Well done (and please fix the bugs)!

title: Great App for Enhancing Task Managers
body:
Great app. I use it as short-term, ad-hoc task management, for core daily repeats, and for doubling down on tasks in my task manager or calendar that I need some nagging on. This keeps my Things task manager and calendar cleaner and encourages me to manage talks I might not log due to time it takes in other apps.

If you get annoyed figuring out if you want something in Due, Reminders, Notes, Things, Calendar, all of them, etc. I highly recommend Drafts, my new favorite iOS app. It allows quick note capture and two tap publish to a large list of apps, including Due. It also allows tweeting. Is it a task, event, idea, tweet, or beginning of a blog post? Decide after you write it. Drafts will also allow multiple sends if you want your text in multiple apps.

My two requests for Due- I wish the 1min default snooze could be 5- it's not useful at 1min and 1hr only. 1min distracts, and I have to turn of the alarm (or reschedule, but then there is no snooze). Also a "send to calendar" or other apps (Reminders, Things) would be nice.

title: Adequate, But Looking for Something Better
body:

First, the out-of-the-box settings result in it nagging you incessantly, and the default due time is two minutes in the future. So you have to go diving into settings, but only after you realise the thing is driving you nuts with its nagging. 

Second, the user interface has that common affliction nowadays - it tries to look minimalist and slick. This comes about from having too many propeller-heads designing things without input from real users. Consequently there's far to many darned buttons to push to do a simple thing like set up a reminder or reschedule it.

title: Timers and reminders done well
body:
You never think of your house chores as of structured work projects, but still need to deliver on time.

Sometimes you don't need to create a project or a task for something that you simply need to do at the right time.

Often you miss a task because you didn't look at your task list at the right time and you missed your time window.

You always have your iPhone or iPad with you.

So all of this means that all you need is to: 

1. Tap a plus sign.
2. Enter a reminder title
3. Slide a couple of dials with several useful presets to set the time
4. Confirm

If you have the app on your Mac with iCloud sync on, you have a reminder you cannot miss, at the time you need to do the task.

All of this with a self-explanatory interface.

One of the first 3 apps I install on any new iOS device/install.

UPDATE: after so many years of using this app, I am still enthusiastically recommending it - it helps me never missing medications, chores, taking documents with me, whatever you may think of that you want to take off your mind, but not miss.

title: Rechtzeitig erinnern mit Nachhaken. Jetzt auch prima auf FaltPhone
body:
Diese Erinnerungsfunktion hatte mir gefehlt. Besonders Ereignisse, an die man wiederholt erinnert werden möchte, weil der eingestellte  Zeitpunkt nicht jeden Tag exakt passt. In meinem Fall sehr gut für die Einnahme von Medikamenten. Dann werde ich eben eine halbe Stunde später noch einmal erinnert. Auch die kreative Eingabemöglichkeit der Einstellungen bringt etwas Freude und Effizienz in den nervenden Vorgang "Wiederkehrende Erinnnerungen". Ich nutze die App jetzt auch zunehmend für einmalige Erinnerungen, weil die Eingabe so simpel ist. Zur richtigen Zeit an alles denken kann diese App gut unterstützen.
Neu: Jetzt verwende ich die App schon einige Jahre regelmäßig. 
Für "Heute xy anrufen" hatte ich nie die geeignete Anwendung. 
in due wird damit der Kalender nicht überfrachtet und ich kann die Erinnerung stundenweise weiterschieben, bis die Gelegenheit gekommen ist. 
Auf meiner Apfeluhr, wird die Erinnerung noch dezenter aufs Handgelenk geklopft. 😀
1.11.18: Snooze täglich wäre noch schön.

body: Ich finde sehr angenehm, dass ich einfach lose und unstrukturiert meine Notizen hier reinhauen kann und sie dann, wenn sie anfangen zu nerven (und das tun sie), sortieren kann. Eine Funktion bei der man nach Erinnerungen (aktuelle, oder gespeicherte) suchen kann.

title: Hilfreiche App
body:
Due ist eine hilfreiche App. Ich benutze sie erst wenige Tage auf meinem iPhone. Nun wollte ich sie ebenfalls auf meinem iPad benutzen und meine Eintragungen synchronisieren. 
Dies ist jedoch nicht möglich, da die Funktion „Mit iCloud synchronisieren“ nicht hervorgehoben und anklickbar ist. 
Schade, diese Funktion würde manches vereinfachen. Wenn ich aber für jedes Gerät eine neue iCloud bräuchte, macht das Ganze irgendwie keinen Sinn. 
Es wäre schön, wenn diese Funktion angeglichen werden würde.

- keine Gruppen
- Import aus Reminder, löscht aber dort

Also für meine Wünsche genau 0 Funktionen was nicht schlimm wäre wenn man testen könnte …

title: Top App!
body: Ich Benutze die App schon seit 2 Jahren und habe sie echt lieben gelernt. Die Integration auf IOS, iPadOS, watchOS und macOS klappt perfekt. ich bin seitdem immer top organisiert und vergesse nix mehr. Die Kosten sind schon recht hoch, vor allem mit dem Abonnement und die Einmalzahlung für das MacBook. Aber die App ist super einfach aber effektiv und sie ist, und das ist enorm wichtig, absolut stabil und verlässlich. Toll ist auch das Logbuch, falls man mal was aus Versehen gelöscht haben sollte.  Daher kann ich die App nur empfehlen!
author: SebEv

title: Für wichtige Erinnerungen, die sicherste App im Store
body:
Due verwende ich seit mehreren Jahren für wichtige Aufgaben, an die ich erinnert werden möchte. Mit 100-prozentiger Sicherheit erhält der Nutzer ein Alarmsignal zur gewünschten Zeit. Eine Wiederholung der Erinnerung ist inklusive und sie kommt immer wieder, bis die Aufgabe abgehakt ist. Das verschieben und neu organisieren von Aufgaben ist durch die eingebauten Zeitschalter sehr leicht zu handhaben.

Immer wieder teste ich auch andere Apps für Aufgaben Erinnerungen. Keine, bietet so zuverlässige Erinnerungsfunktionen wie Due.

author: Kleo-Patra

title: Ich bin am Ziel!!
body:
Danke Danke Danke! 

Fast alle bekannten ToDo Apps hab ich getestet. Immer ein paar Wochen und dann doch wieder nicht mehr verwendet. 

Hier ist es anders. Die Kombination aus penetranter Erinnerung und schnellem neuterminieren lässt mich alles erledigen und nichts vergessen. Genau das was ich gesucht habe. Einfach und schnell.
Ich verwende die App seit 14Tagen und es macht so langsam sogar Spaß damit Dinge einzutragen und sie zu erldedigen :)

Warum ich so spät erst getestet habe liegt wohl am Design. Verglichen mit den großen bekannten Produktivitätsapps bleibt man leider beim Scrollen im App Store nicht direkt hängen. Einem einzelnen ToDo kann ich ebenfalls auch nicht so viel anhängen, in so fern probiert man erst anderes, aber ich hab gemerkt ich brauch keine ToDos mit Bildern, Listen, Emojis und dem ganzen anderen Kladderadatsch.

Fazit: Daumen hoch.
author: belo2011

title: Kaum mehr Änderungen im Text möglich
body:
Änderung der Bewertung am 01.12.20

Nach Kontakt mit Appmachern wurde alles geklärt und eine praktikable Lösung angeboten... deshalb revidiere ich meine Bewertung von 1 Stern auf 4 von 5 Sternen!

Es ist kaum mehr möglich Text / Buchstaben in bereits angelegten Erinnerungen zu ändern (ios 14.2.1, iphone 12) . Es wird überwiegend ein ganzes Wort markiert und das läßt sich auch nicht einzeln löschen oder beim Versuch es zu ändern stürzt DUE ab. Macht keinen Spaß mehr und nervt total.

Wer nur die Basics ohne Abo nutzt: gut und praktisch

Ich gebe nur zwei Punkte, da Features, für die man extra Geld verlangt, auch funktionieren sollten.

title: Diese App zeigt, wieviel Potential in Erinnerungen steckt!
body:
An der regulären Erinnerungs-App hat mich stets eine Sache gewaltig gestört: Ist eine Erinnerung fällig, so gibt es zum Fälligkeitszeitpunkt eine Benachrichtigung. Das war‘s. Klickt man diese Benachrichtigung weg, oder übersieht sie, so wird man nicht erneut an die fällige Erinnerung erinnert. 

Due setzt genau hier an. Ist eine Erinnerung fällig, so werden in wählbaren Zeitabständen solange neue Benachrichtigungen erzeugt, bis die Erinnerung in der App als Erledigt markiert wurde. Mir hilft das ungemein meine fälligen Termine im Blick zu halten. 
Außerdem ersetzt dies für mich eine separate To-Do-List, da die Erinnerungen in der App schön chronologisch anhand der noch bis zur Fälligkeit verbleibenden Zeit aufgelistet sind.

Und zum Schluss ein Wort zum ‚Abo‘. 
Durch den Kauf dieser App erhält man lebenslangen Zugriff zu allen Funktionen, die diese App zum jetzigen Stand (+ 1 Jahr) besitzt. Ist nach Kaufdatum ein Jahr verstrichen und es werden wesentliche neue Funktionen (nicht lediglich Bug-fixes) hinzugefügt, so müssen diese durch einen erneuten Kauf erworben werden. 
Was man also durch diesen freiwilligen quasi jährlichen Zusatzkauf erhält sind maßgebliche neue Features. Man kann jedoch jederzeit darauf verzichten und die App mit dem derzeitig Stand unbegrenzt nutzen. Für mich ein absolut faires Modell, was den Entwicklern auch einen Anreiz bietet, die App noch Jahre später weiter zu entwickeln und zu adaptieren!

title: Gute Idee – fehlerhafter Sync
body:
1 Stern, weil die App aus (nicht nachvollziehbaren) Gründen mal synchronisiert, mal nicht ... und deshalb manchmal schlicht durch „Multialarme“ nervt. 
Vorab: Die Idee und die Umsetzung der App sind prima, wenn man sich etwas in die Einstellmöglichkeiten eingearbeitet hat. Dafür gäbe es 4 Sterne (einen Stern Abzug für Probleme mit dem Standardalarm).
Ärgerlich bis hochgradig nervig ist die mangelhafte (Hintergrund)Synchronisierung zwischen iOS-Geräten. Ob iCloud oder Dropbox (beides mehrfach probiert): Auf einem Device als „erledigt“ abgehakte Reminder „klingeln“ auf dem anderen (manchmal - nicht immer?) solange munter weiter, bis die App auf beiden Geräten zeitgleich im Vordergrund aktiviert wurde. 
In Terminen oder bei Telefonaten ist das extrem störend.
Das Problem scheint bekannt(? / zusammenhängend mit der „iOS Aufwachfunktion“ einer App?).
Die native (kostenlose) iOS-Erinnerung beherrscht diesen Sync. Da dies eine Grundfunktion/ßvoraussetzung ist, kann es bis auf weiteres für eine kostenpflichtige Erinneruns-App nur einen Stern geben. Leider.

title: Endlich mit Hintergrundaktualisierung
body:
Die meistbenutzte App auf meinem iPhone. Großes Lob und vielen Dank an den Programmierer. Ohne diese App würde ich sicher viele wichtige Dinge vergessen. Das wiederkehrende Erinnerungsfenster bei fälligen Aufgaben ist einfach genial. Jetzt endlich mit Hintergrundaktualisierung. Änderungen am Mac werden jetzt wirklich am iPhone durchtransportiert, auch wenn das iPhone im Standby ist. Dann bimmelt nicht ständig das iPhone, obwohl die Aufgabe am Mac schon längst als erledigt markiert wurde. Tolles neues Tool, um Zeiten zu pflegen. Weiter so.

Update 10.10.2016

Nach iOS10 leider nur noch Probleme. Reminder, die auf der AppleWatch angezeigt werden, lassen sich auf der AppleWatch nur schwer als erledigt kennzeichnen. Die App auf der Uhr friert irgendwie ständig ein. Wenn es dann doch mal gelingt, einen Reminder auf erledigt zu setzen, bekomme ich ständig weiter Erinnerungen, dass ich noch etwas zu erledigen habe. Grund ist, dass das auf erledigt-Setzten auf der AppleWatch nicht bis zum iPhone durchgedrungen ist. Dort kommt das nicht an und die Reminder bleiben dort unerledigt. Sehr nervig. Außerdem friert auch Due auf dem iPhone sehr oft ein oder stürzt ab. Die Hintergrundaktualisierung vom Mac zum iPhone über DropBox wird auf dem iPhone auch nicht im Hintergrund ausgeführt. Diese Funktion ist völlig funktionslos. Bitte dringen nachbessern.

Update 03.08.2017

So, der Hintergrundsync vom Mac zum iPhone läuft endlich wieder rund seit der Version 2.5. Das war leider in der Vergangenheit etwas ins Stottern geraten.
Und, die Komplikation läuft auch super auf der Apple Watch. Die DueApp auf der Apple Watch synchronisiert jetzt viel schneller mit dem iPhone als vorher. Das gefällt mir ganz besonders gut. Die Wartezeiten vorher waren ein Unding. Jetzt läufts geschmeidig.

Update 29.08.2018

Bin sehr froh, dass diese App noch immer sehr gepflegt wird. Das kostenpflichtige Update auf 3.0 ist mehr als gerechtfertigt. Wenn damit sichergestellt wird, dass die App nicht lieblos aufgegeben wird, bin ich gern bereit, hier weiter zu zahlen. Denn e werden ja auch neue Funktionen geliefert. Also es ist kein Abo allein des Verdienens wegen.

Perfekte App!

title: App dank Support leider nur eine 5
body:
Nachtrag : Der Support hat immer noch nicht geantwortet, die App funktioniert immer noch nicht, wie sie es mal tat und tuen sollte! Also, nur 2 Sterne weil Note mangelhaft ! Eigentlich eine 6 aber man hofft ja noch etwas ! 

Die App ist toll, klasse und hilft. Außer ein paar Dingen, die diese App perfekt machen könnten ist die neu integrierte Hintergrundaktualisiering wohl nur ein Gedanken beim verfassen der Beschreibung gewesen! 
Ich habe es bis heute nicht geschafft, das DUE bei allen Erlaubnissen für Hintergrund, Dropbox usw. im Hintergrund die Daten aktuell hat ! 
Das nervt ! Soll die App ja auch damit man die Dinge auch erledigt, die man dort eingetragen hat, aber hier passiert nüscht, nix, einfach gar nichts ! 
3 Geräte, 3x akt. iOS, 3x immer GSM Netz meist UMTS, sonst WLAN mit 11.5 Mbps/8.9 Mbps ! Aber DUE überträgt einfach die Daten nicht ! Toll, wenn zB das iPad hinten in der Tasche ist und man im Auto fährt und man nicht dran kommt ! Selbst nach 38h hat das iPad was noch im Büro lag, immer noch den alten Bestand, erst wenn man es öffnet, dann fängt es an zu synchronisieren! Habe denn nur ich diesen nervigen Fehler ?

title: Was soll ich sagen?? Eigentlich ganz schickes update,aber
body:
Nun ich habe das Update nun einige Zeit getestet. Es funktioniert super und sieht sehr Zeit gemäss aus. Allerdings wurden viele funktionen verschlimmbessert wie u.a.

- zu viele umständliche Buttons. Früher genügte ein Klick und die Aufgabe war bespielsweise um 10 Min verschoben. Heute erscheint ein unübersichtliches Pop-Up Fenster wo  12 verschiedene Buttons drin sind.

- Wiederholungen einstellen war mal einfach, heute umständlich.

- gruppierung der aufgaben macht es unübersichtlich ( heute, morgen, nächste Woche)

- sync zwischen IPhone/IPad und mac funktionierte bei mir über die icloud noch nie zuverläßig.

- timer pausieren und fortsetzen, welches eigentlich eine Grundfunktionalität sein sollte und auch war, ist heute auf einmal ein In-App-feature <--- a joke, right??

- Backgroundsync NUR über Dropbox möglich....und nicht über ICloud

Besonders traurig ist das der entwickler leider nicht auf meine Anfragen reagiert hat.

Ich habe allerdings nichts gegen den In-App kauf, ich denke das ist im großen und ganzen ok. Schließlich hat er viel arbeit investiert und hätte die neue Version auch als neue App anbieten können, so wie es viele andere auch tun. 

Was ich jedoch unverschämt finde ist, dass er mir jetzt Standard-Timer-Funktionen unterschlägt obwohl diese vorher vorhanden waren!!

Alles im allen hätte ich gerne die alte Version zurück, da diese viel produktiver und schneller war

Edit 16.4.2015: ICloud sync zwischen Mac und Iphone version funktioniert nicht mehr. Die Mac Version erkennt die vorhandene Datenbank vom IPhone nicht mehr. Selbst ein löschen und neu hochladen der Datenbank ist keine Lösung!!! Echt traurig, soll ich etwa zu dem Inapp- kauf gezwungen werden??

title: Great App BUT
body:
Ich nutze die App jetzt schon viele Monate und hatte bis jetzt nie etwas zu bemängeln. Ganz im Gegenteil, ich fand es war eine der gelungensten Apps und habe sie Freunden empfohlen. Das neue Design mag Geschmacksache sein. Mir persönlich bringt es keinen nennenswerten Mehrwert, aber es stört mich auch nicht sonderlich.

Der eingentliche Grund warum ich diese Bewertung schreibe und die App leider von einer 5 auf eine 2 abstufe ist folgender: Ich finde es vollkommen inakzeptabel wenn sich App Developer entscheiden Funktionen die vorher für Bestandskunden inklusive waren als neu zu verkaufen und somit versuchen bestehende Kunden nochmals zur Kasse zu bitten. Ist ja nicht der Fehler des Kunden, dass der Developer Scheins falsch kalkuliert hat und jetzt merkt, dass ein bisschen extra Cash Flow eine nette Sache wären. Ganz besonders ärgerlich ist es im Fall von Due, da kleine essentielle Features wie z.B das pausieren von einem Timer (die vorher Teil der App waren) nun als in-App-Kauf wieder erworben werden sollen. Bei einer Erweiterung um gute neue Features entlohne ich den Entwickler sehr gerne für seine Arbeit, aber ganz bestimmt nicht dafür das Vertrauen seiner Kunden zu brechen. Wirklich schade.

title: Wer kennt Alternative?
body:

Grund 1:
Früher konnte man blind Erinnerungen (vor allem wiederkehrende) nach hinten verschieben. Jetzt muss man höllisch aufpassen, dass man nicht die komplette Terminserie verändert. 1 Sekunde nicht aufgepasst und Peng!!!

Grund 2:
Früher war es nicht möglich, einen Termin einfach zu löschen. Wenn man nun leicht nach links wischt, ist die Aufgabe erledigt. Wischt man ein bisschen zu weit, wird die komplette Aufgabe gelöscht. 
Das ist wirklich heftig, weil auch wiederkehrende Erinnerungen versehentlich viel zu leicht gelöscht werden können.

Früher war die App leicht, einfach zu bedienen, übersichtlich. Jetzt kann man nur davon abraten.

title: Sehr zu empfehlen!!!
body:
Ich benutze Due schon eine ganze Weile (2 oder 3 Jahre) und war recht zufrieden, obwohl es  nicht ganz optimal war. Ich muss gestehen, dass ich dazu aber kein Feedback an den Entwickler gegeben habe :-(.
Umso erstaunter war ich, dass mit der Version 2.0 eigentlich alle Punkte, die mich störten, überarbeitet wurden und Due für mich nun ganz nah am Optimum ist!! Due ist für mich die App, die ich am häufigsten verwende. 

Zu den Punkten, die mir wichtig sind:
- die Eingabe neuer Erinnerungen ist sehr einfach, trotz der vielen Möglichkeiten. 
- aktuelle Erinnerungen zu verschieben geht nun noch leichter mit einem Menü, das die verschiedenen Optionen übersichtlich anzeigt. 
- das neue Layout (iPhone 6) ist sehr gelungen und übersichtlich gestaltet. 
- die Synchronisation über IOS Geräte hinweg funktioniert nun automatisch. 

Die Kosten für das Upgrade habe ich gerne bezahlt. Der Entwickler hat sich wirklich viele Gedanken gemacht und es dürfte eine Menge Arbeit darin stecken. 

Und sollte ich Ideen haben, wie sich Due noch weiter verbessern lässt, dann werde ich sie in Zukunft auch dem Entwickler zukommen lassen :-).

title: Schöne Idee..
body:
...noch etwas unfertig,aber das kann ja noch werden. 

Top ist:

- die "nervende" Erinnerung,für mich genial...andere Reminder cancel ich und vergesse die Erledigung. Diese hier "vergisst" man nicht...;-)!

- die kleinen sich immer wiederholenden Erinnerungen,einfacher Zugriff...Top. 

Negativ leider die Texterkennung!So gut wie sie am Mac funktioniert,so schlecht arbeitet sie hier. Es ist nicht zu schaffen,eine Erinnerung mit Freitext einzugeben,ohne das diese in den nächsten Minuten startet. Obwohl dies eigentlich erst morgen oder in einer Woche passieren sollte!

Hab mit dem Entwickler Kontakt aufgenommen und das Problem geschildert. Hat sich ziemlich gewunden,auf die Unterschiede von ios und Mac OSX verwiesen und eigentlich sollte es ja gehen....tja tut es leider nicht!

3 Sterne für die tolle Idee,aber da ist noch Luft nach oben.

title: Perfekt... Und jetzt auch mit iCloud-Sync
body:
Due war vor dem Update schon sehr gut, mit dem iCloud-Sync und der Optimierung für das neue iPad ist es für mich noch einen Tick besser. 

Die App konzentriert sich weiterhin auf das Wesentliche: schnell und einfach eine Aufgabe anlegen, bei Bedarf auch als Serie z. B. mit Wiederholung pro Woche, Monat etc. und erinnert einen dann mit (einstellbarer) Penetranz. ;)

Wer für seine Aufgaben Ordnerstrukturen, ausgefeilte Abhängigkeiten von anderen Aufgaben oder massenweise Informationen wie z. B. Dateianhänge benötigt, wird mit Due nicht glücklich werden. 

Wer es einfach haben möchte und ein zuverlässiges Helferlein für viele, kleine schnell anzulegende aber eben auch nicht zu vergessende Aufgaben benötigt: Kaufen!!!

title: Da fehlt noch was....
body:
Genervt von Things (und auf der ewigen Suche nach einem wirklich praktischen(!), einfachen(!) Tool) nun also bei Due gelandet. Auf den ersten Blick gut, praktische Funktionen, klare, einfache Gliederung.
Leider kann es für mich Things doch noch nicht ersetzen, denn die Möglichkeiten wiederholbarer Erinnerungen sind zu schwach: Es geht lediglich täglich, wöchentlich und jeden Monat.
Termine, die z.B. quartalsweise oder jährlich anfallen - Fehlanzeige. Aber das Teil ist ja noch relativ neu, vielleicht wird das ja noch...

Ach ja: Wiederholbare Erinnerungen verschwinden erstmal, wenn sie sich erledigt haben. Das empfinde ich als unübersichtlich. Hier wäre es ideal, einen eigenen Hauptpunkt zu haben, also neben "Erinnerungen / Timer / Logbuch" noch einen weiteren Punkt "Wiederholungen".
Unter diesem Punkt sollten dann alle wiederholbaren Erinnerungen verwaltet werden können.

Und was natürlich auch praktisch wäre: Wenn man den Erinnerungen einem Label zuordnen könnte, um z.B. alle Geschäftstermine filtern zu können.

Dann wäre das Teil für mich total genial...... Daher erstmal 3 Sterne.

title: Haz tus tareas en el momento adecuado.
body:
Para mi, Due app es una genial app de alarma, que te permite programar alarmas, avisos, programar temporizadores, etc.
Por fin una manera de recordar esas tareas que debes hacer con un horario determinado.
La aplicación tiene mucho que ofrecer, por lo que conviene escarbar entre sus opciones y visitar la web del desarrollador para sacar el máximo partido posible a la app, así como conocer las limitaciones de esta.
Due pretende ser una aplicación de alarma, que en pocos pasos te permite programar alarmas y recordatorios de manera más rápida que la aplicación por defecto que viene en el iPhone, aunque después de esta última actualización, la app pierde velocidad al presentar nuevos menús al tocar sobre las opciones que nos permiten definir el tipo de alarma que queremos que suene, así como el snooze, etc.
Otra de las cualidades de esta app es la de poder hacer backups de nuestras alarmas, así como la de sincronizarlas a través de dropbox con otros dispositivos.
Una buena compra.
Recomendada y ahora además universal.

Actualización 202-01-29
La sincronización en segundo plano sigue fallando entre dispositivos. Una vez salta una alarma en iphone y la paras, sigue sonando en el ipad. 
Eso no debería pasar.

title: Not worth it.
body:
I bought this app because I thought it’s gonna be perfect. Expectations vs Reality as they call it. I’ve been using another Calendar / Reminder that’s called “Timetree” it’s free. But then, I saw this “Due reminder app” as a suggested app in appstore, and I immediately fell inlove with the interface that was shown in the pictures. So I bought it for 6€. I didn’t mind paying for it because I thought it’s worth it. But... I just thought it. Not only that it’s not worth it of it’s price but also lots of lacking. The previous app that I was using, It has an option that it can remind you the reminder 1 or more days, weeks or months before the said date. The due app should have that kind of option because it’s a reminder app. But no, it only has an “over due” option which is I find useless in my opinion. 
It’s not a friendly user. I tried a lot of samples to see maybe I wasn't just used to using it or I didn't know how to use it and it’s just not that good. Also, it would be really helpful if they add a widget and the future / advance notification for the upcoming event / reminder. 
I’m far from satisfied with my purchase.

title: Muy buena idea pero falta mejorar.
body:
Sorprendentemente en el mundo iPhone parece ser que tanto en calendario como en tareas... 

los avisos, si los pillas bien, y si no, también... 

Ni el propio iPhone persiste bien en los avisos,  ni el 99% de las APP de terceros. Nadie lo tiene en cuenta. 

Esta App si. Programas una tarea para que emita un sonido personalizado a tal hora, por ejemplo tomarte una pastilla. Si no haces ni dices nada te vuelve a avisar cada x minutos que hayas definido en la tarea. Por tanto es muy difícil que no lo pilles. Luego cuando sale el aviso puedes marcar para que avise de nuevo en un tiempo estandard o que de la tarea por terminada. Hasta aquí perfecto por que  es muy eficiente. No necesitas ni abrir la app en semanas. 

Pero: 
1) Al definir una nueva tarea tienes que adivinar demasiado: siempre tienes dudas de si Ok quiere decir terminado o bien guardar cambios. 
2) Cuando sale el aviso debería dar opción a pedir cuando debe volver a avisar. Si programo para hacer copia de seguridad a las cuatro y que me insista cada 15 minutos, bien si estoy en casa. Sigo con mi café y si me olvido, a los 15 minutos me vuelve a avisar, pero si estoy en el cine es un fastidio, o la doy por terminada o sale el aviso 50 veces hasta que llego a casa. En el cine me gustaría decir avisame en tres horas. 
3) No conecta con el outlook ni con las tareas del iPhone. 
4) Al programar tareas repetitivas son de un día para otro. Si se pudiera poner repetición durante el día a x y z horas con fecha inicio y final seria muy útil para tratamientos medicos. Y estaría muy bien porque con esta app no te olvidas de nada. 
5) Puesto que no hay dicha repetición estaría bien que hubiera un botón para duplicar tareas, seria un copiar pegar editar en uno. 
6) Debería haber un botón para inhabilitar/habilitar tareas ya que hay tareas que en verano o en vacaciones no las haces pero cuando vuelves si

En fin, critica constructiva destinada a mejorar

title: Excellente application sur IPhone !
body:
Août 2018 : 
Toujours excellent. Utilisation quotidienne ! 

Septembre 2017 : 
Toujours excellent. Sauvegarde automatique améliorée, voire parfaite. Paramétrages multiples. C'est l'application que j'utilise le plus, après "Notes" et "Google maps". 

Mars 2016 : toujours "fidèle" à cette application qui me rend beaucoup de services, tous les jours et plusieurs fois par jour ! Les améliorations de cette dernière années ont apportées de vraies facilités (ergonomie, fonctionnalités). 

Avril 2014 sur IPhone : c'est l'application que j'utilise le plus souvent (plusieurs fois par jour) avec Week Cal, depuis trois ans, déjà ! 
Sans erreurs, je n'ai plus rien oublié (:-)) depuis des mois ! Car le Pop-up de l'application me le rappelle sans cesse toutes les minutes, avec petit son discret et sympa et/ou "petite vibration" (dans le cas où l'Iphone serait sur mode silencieux dans une poche. Ré configurer  une nouvelle alerte (10min plus tard, 1h plus tard, 1 jour plus tard) de la même tâche se fait en (seulement) deux gestes.

Bravo encore !

14juin 2011 : 
Excellente application. 
Après avoir essayé d'autres "to do", rappels et minuteurs divers, je pense avoir trouvé ce qu'il me fallait : simplicité, ergonomie, esthétique, configuration. 

Petite suggestion : pourquoi ne pas pouvoir configurer rappels > répétitions > personnaliser > dans heures et minutes, aussi ? 
(Il est vrai que le minuteur de cette application fait très bien cela)

Bravo et merci !

title: Really well executed app
body:
Really nicely done app. The way you can schedule events with natural language is nice, the various notification and delay options are great, and it feels like the developer really cared about creating a great experience. 

For years I’ve used my calendar as a todo list for important things, adding events when I think I might tackle it, but it’s a pain to keep on top of and if you miss an event you have to remember to manually reschedule. This app is basically the structure version of that workflow - items have times (super easy to enter), it reminds you at the time and also makes it trivial to defer by whatever time unit you like. 

My one very slight nit is I would love an option to use the standard iOS system font. The one it uses is fine and easy to read, I just like things to look consistent in general. But that’s a minor issue with an otherwise great app. Nice work.

title: Should be called “Nag” not “Due”
body:
I’ve used this app for at least 2 years now, and belatedly just realised I don’t just dislike this app, I despise it with every fibre of my being, so much so I have realised it is actually bad for my mental health. This app doesn’t remind you about stuff, it nags you and nags you and nags you until you want to scream! In the middle of a phone call? nag nag nag, obviously busy and not responding? nag nag nag. Pay “me attention” is its constant refrain, it like having a rude and badly behaved 4 yr old child in your pocket - permanently! I felt stressed every morning when my list of “nags” would start harassing me as soon as I woke up. If I had 2 nags go off at the same time I get double notifications simultaneously! Double nagging OMG! Even Apples restricted notifications don’t seem to be able to shut it up. I’ve actually thrown my phone at the wall because of its constant nagging.

There is literally nothing positive I can find to say about this app, even the “Undo edit reminder” is stupidly placed so that pressing the screen off button “undoes” your changes with the palm of your hand without realising it. 1 minute later you get nagged about the same thing all over again!

 I finally realised yesterday, this app doesn’t help me get stuff done, it just stresses me out about everything I’ve not got around to today, and loads up trepidation about tomorrow. I would willing burn every byte that belongs to this app, sadly I will just have to make do with “delete”.

title: Due done & dusted
body:
I pontificated long over purchasing Due, especially as I was already using one of the market leaders (OmniFocus). We tend to forget just how convenient it is to have everything synced across all devices. However sync is the only bugbear for me with Due. 

I set a due time on say my phone, then change it on my iPad and that updated information doesn’t get updated on the other devices so someone else in the house or office will be complaining that the phone has been going off every few minutes even though the actual time was updated.

I even had one reminder that went off a day and a half early, I’m sure it was correctly set, its a bit odd. Slightly disappointing.

If they could get the sync sorted on iCloud it would be a real winner. Until then I wouldn’t trust it for anything really critical.

author: emeliaphil

title: This is perfection
body:
Apple’s reminders in iOS 13 just got worse with the lack of days of the week on the scroll wheel - so I went looking for something that worked in an intuitive, logical user friendly manner - Due fulfilled that criteria and oh so much more!
I will not be able to fully do this app justice here, but to add a little weight to how grateful I am to the creators of this app, I can tell you this is the only review I ever written in my life... about anything.

The various ways in which one can enter the timings for the reminder is wonderful; partly because it is easy, fast, so ‘end user’ practical and highly customisable; allowing for different people’s preferences and yet clean, clear and simple. It also enabled me to import my existing reminders from the Apple Reminders app - which is very useful because some of my reminders are not so much time related - just when I get an idea for something I jot it down as a reminder so I can add a date and time if I need to later.
I think intuitive intelligence went into the making of this app.

I’m going to finish waffling by saying - if you need a wonderful one time purchase (which is important to me) reminders app then get this - it just works! And even if Apple are clever enough to add days of the week! into their reminders app... I won’t be going back to it. I wish I’d found this years ago.

And to the creators... thank you so very much.

title: Remind me to write a review about Due!
body:
With this app you’ll never forget anything that’s really important ever again. Just add it to Due and it will be taken care of. There are so many nagging options so use this app with attention. I don’t add all my reminders to it, although that is an option too. Just the ones that are important one-offs plus some simple repeating tasks. 

The app now has the best subscription model available. Pay a small amount for a year and whatever new is added before your subscription runs out is to keep, even if you decide not to renew.  I am looking forward to some cool things being added to this app in the near future. New Shortcuts have just been added. Great.
 
I must also mention the Watch app. It’s so useful. Every time Due wants to remind me of something I get a tap on my wrist. Again, and again, and again. I can mark the task off, snooze it, or reschedule it. I can also set a task from my wrist if I feel like it. 

This app is THE best at what it does. I am very happy that I can support this developer with a small subscription each year.

title: iOS app great, WatchOS app useless
body:
Edit: 2020-01-23 (previous review at bottom)

Indispensable. Helps me get through the day by reminding my addled brain to do all those little things that would otherwise fall by the wayside. If it’s something that occurs with a repeatable pattern, I probably have it in Due. 

Pleased to report that the Watch companion app now behaves beautifully too. 

===

Previous review
—
The iOS app is great, I'd give it five stars, although the recent changes in iOS to the number of notifications have not been good for Due. Sometimes, "nag" reminders just stop. Otherwise great. 

The WatchOS app is a total waste of time, to the extent that I'd advise anyone buying with the intention of relying on the Watch app not to waste their money. Most of the time, the app is unresponsive, and completing reminders and stopping timers, when the app does work, is a lottery. It is one of those cases where you're better off using normal Watch notifications rather than this very poor Watch app. 1 star.

So, an average of three stars, then. I'll revisit this if the developer improves the WatchOS performance.

title: Nags me (in a good way)
body:
I have a problem with standard alarm apps; if I'm in the middle of something and they go off, I will dismiss them, finish what I was doing, then forget that the alarm had gone off. Yes, even if it only takes me a minute to finish what I was doing - because then something else will get my attention, then something else, and so on.

What's great about Due is that it gently nags me. It just politely goes "ping" then shuts up for a minute. Then it goes "ping" again, and I think "yeah, yeah, nearly done". Then it goes "ping" again, I finish up and there's my reminder on the lock screen. It doesn't buzz and jingle and beg for attention until I tell it to shut up, so I can ignore it until I'm ready.  And if I know I'm not going to be able to do the task for a while, it's blindingly quick to snooze it for a few minutes, hours or days.

I use this app dozens of times in a day. Very very useful.

title: Sync is a joke and developer doesn't care
body:
Great looking app and if you live in a world where you only have one device then it is perfect.

I don't live in that world and after spending a lot of time trying to get things to work it is clear that the current app can't support downloading changes made on other devices automatically.

iCloud complains of error 260 and Dropbox works well to sync when the app is running.

title: Great, but a couple of crucial limitations
body:
This is a great app - I've just bought it for both iOS and Mac OS, and it synchronises and does everything it's supposed to. The crucial flaw as I see it at this stage is that the iOS version only synchronises (I'm using Dropbox as the sync method - I've no idea if it behaves the same using iCloud as the sync method) when you open and close the app. 

All the reminders work fine when the app isn't working - I get all the notifications and everything. But if I mark a reminder as complete on my Mac, that isn't synchronised with the iOS version until I open it. That's the crucial flaw. The whole purpose of a seamless reminders app (which this is in virtually every other respect) is that you don't have to put effort into doing it - it should do it for you. Devs, please please fix it so that it updates live in the background, so I never need to actually open the app on my iDevice except to create new reminders or mark old ones as done. If I have to remember to open it to make sure my reminders are up to date - what's the point?

The only other complaint I have is the default 'snooze' times in iOS - 1 minute or 1 hour is very limited compared to the broad range of times available in Mac OS. However, I know the devs are aware of this one and are working on it, so it's a 'for now' complaint only. 

Other than that, it's brilliant - I love the "do x tomorrow" and it'll mark it for 9am, or "do it in one hour" or "do it at 4". Lovely, very refreshing and simple and quick. The only other thing I would suggest is have voice-recognition - how much easier would it be to have all those features but just SAY to your iPhone "wake me up tomorrow at 6am" or something like that. Perhaps Apple will allow Siri integration in iOS 6… who knows?

Great app all in all - needs a bit more to make it all that it could be though.

title: Essential features modifications required.
body:
Don't get me wrong, this is a great program, but it needs a couple of features to be modified.

Over a year ago, I personally contacted the developer about this. He said that he would modify the features for the next build. The mods didn't materialise, hence this poor review.

I will rewrite this review when my requests have materialised.

The modified features requested were - and are: the requests are still needed.

1. The repeated reminder alarm feature for the reminders feature needs to have more variable time limits. It is not up to the job: the time period options are either too long, or too short.

Along with the repeat options of 1 minute and 1 hour, the following default options are required:

1. 5 mins
2. 10 mins
3. 20 mins
4. 30 mins
5. 45 mins

The other modification urgently required is more time allowed to quickly change the default snooze if needed.

I would like to see the automatic hiding function removed from the additional options for the reminder being modified.

There is no need to hide it automatically AND it's very annoying whilst modifying a current alarm to have it beeping away at you AND disappearing whist you are trying to get in with it.

This review is solely to spur the developer to fix these issues. This is otherwise a good program - it just needs some attention.

title: Due.App is a good "deadline" reminder App, But a poor "Nag" reminder App
body:
I would classify Due.App as an "Impending-reminder.App"  for imminent/urgent tasks   (Impending=about to happen). 

I have 2 needs for this type of App :- 

PURPOSE 1. Deadline reminder - time critical (continuous nag alarm every 1 minute)  
PURPOSE 2. Nag reminder (Nag alarms with a range of minute & hours options)

Due.App is a very good "deadline" reminder App, But a poor "Nag" reminder App.
I can set a reminder to nag every 1 minute or every 1 hour but nothing in between and so Due.App is too basic to be used as a "Nag" reminder app 

N.B Other Deadline reminder apps are nag.app  or EasyReminders.app
N.B. Other "NAG" reminder Apps (which meet the criteria above) are beep-me.app, nagger.app and alarmed.app (yoctoville -use the DayMinder feature and make sure preference>dayminder super user is switched on) 
 
If you make this preference:-
Settings > When adding reminders > Default snooze > None,  then you won't be tied to a global setting of 1 minute or 1 hour. You will be able to make the choice once they're created (click zzzz button)

title: The Only App That Keeps Me from Switching iPhone
body:
If you are someone who frequently forgets tasks—even when using Apple Reminders or other task-management apps—this solution is for you. Its standout feature is persistent alerts that continue to remind you until the task is completed. It also offers flexible options for postponing tasks at your convenience, giving you full control.

One of the most impressive aspects is its clean, intuitive user interface. You can create or modify a task and set the time in just a matter of seconds. Another valuable feature is that you don’t need to open the app to review pending tasks; the app proactively ensures that each task is addressed. The only requirement is a one-time setup.

In short, this is the only app that keeps me from switching to the productivity powerhouse, the Samsung Ultra. Unfortunately, it is available only on the iOS platform.

Tips for Using the App More Efficiently:

Because the reminders can be frequent, you may sometimes find them intrusive. However, this feature is essential to help you stay on track. To manage this, I created an Apple iOS Focus mode that prevents Due alerts from appearing immediately and instead sends them directly to the Notification Center and Lock Screen. This way, I can review alerts whenever I check my phone, without being interrupted by constant notifications.

title: This is THE APP for scheduling reminders!
body: I just love this app. If you’re looking for an app specifically for reminders, this is it. It has the ability to partition reminders into sections: overdue, today, tomorrow, next 7 days and future. On scheduling reminders, say if a reminder is just less than a month away, it’ll say <4 weeks. I would also rate the snooze feature as “intelligent”, if you don’t hear the reminder ring and miss the snooze, say if you’re phone’s on silent, the reminder goes into overdue and will keep giving you a chance to snooze again on intervals you set, 1, 5, 10, 15, 30 minutes or hourly or choose to switch off snooze. I highly recommend this app!

title: Bug
body:
There is a bug parsing Italian complex relative times. For example if I want to say "Cena fra 2 ore e 15 minuti" for a dinner that will be after 2 hours AND 15 minutes from now, the app will set a timer in 15 minutes, ignoring 2 hours. I tried also "Cena fra 2 ore, 15 minuti" or "cena fra 2 ore: 15 minuti", "Cena fra 2 ore + 15 minuti".
There is no difference between Italian words "tra" or "fra", but for Due 3 with "tra" natural parsing is ignored.
There is also a translate error "Oggi + in ritarto" in options about badge icon: in correct Italian the app must say "Oggi + in ritardo" (a D instead of a T).
Add possibility to create a timer from apple watch like the native timer app does.
However thanks for your great app, good job!

title: Non condivide i dati con il Promemoria integrato
body:
Con la 2.0, molto più pulita e con nuove opzioni (ma solo a pagamento, perché?), qualche passo in avanti ma...non condivide ancora i dati con il Promemoria integrato IOS. Non credo sia complicato visto che altre app lo fanno!!! Così non va. Scritto allo sviluppatore ma mai ricevuta risposta. La parte relativa ai Timers non in linea con il resto, sembra far parte di un applicazione diversa, brutta e poco funzionale (andrebbe aggiornata e resa molto più gradevole. La concorrente Timer+ è di un'altra categoria). Una stella in attesa di miglioramenti e in quanto non iCloud based reminder.

Vecchia recensione.
Interfaccia poco pulita, non in linea con IOS 7, manca personalizzazione tempo snooze. Ma cosa più importante... non condivide i dati con il Promemoria integrato IOS, il che lo rende inutile, mentre altre app lo fanno (es: GoodTask). Sopravvalutato!!!

title: Ottima, ma la grafica iOS7?
body:
Aggiornamento al 28/12/2013

Ma la grafica iOS7 Style? Tolgo un'altra stelletta perché non è possibile che nel frattempo App come allarmed (gratuita!) si siano aggiornate e questa resti così. 

Per il resto, se non amate la grafica di iOS 7 oppure non badate all'estetica, allora vale sempre questa recensione fatta a suo tempo: 

Da "praticante" fedelissimo del GTD di David Allen, cercavo qualcosa che fosse "nel mezzo" tra Things (App n. 1 per il GTD, la quale per la sua logica non ha e non deve avere "allarmini") e il calendario. 

Dopo aver investito circa una decina di euro per provare un bel po' di App di reminder, posso dire A VOCE ALTA che questa è la numero 1: grafica bella e pulita, logica di funzionamento che richiede un'oretta di pratica ma che poi diventa STRAORDINARIA PER LA SUA VELOCITÀ. Cosa dire? Se state cercando un App che vi ricordi delle scadenze ad ora e data precisa (o ricorrenze) e soprattutto con pochi click volete poter utilizzare uno snooze reimpostabile, non troverete di meglio. A proposito di snooze è inammissibile che sia impostabile ad un minuto o un'ora è manchi la possibilità di impostare 5, 10 e 15 minuti. Quando ci sarà avrà le 5 stelle.

title: Buoni i timer, inutili i promemoria
body:
L'ho comprata perché volevo dei promemoria ricorrenti che non andassero spuntanti come fatti (volevo solo che ad un certo orario ogni tot giorni mi apparisse una notifica con un suono). Invece nella parte promemoria:
- se non si spuntano i promemoria ricorrenti poi non li segnala le volte successive
- lo snooze ogni ora è inutile perché passa troppo tempo
- lo snooze ad un minuto è veramente assillante e si rischia di rompere l'iPhone per il nervosismo che porta
- non si possono personalizzare le durate degli snooze 
- i suoni non sono il massimo

Trovo utile invece i timer:
-si possono tenere in memoria pronti per essere attivati più timer (come ad esempio è con le sveglie dell'app orologio
-si possono attivare più timer contemporaneamente
-si possono impostare timer che si comportino poi come sveglia (suonino e richiedano di essere staccati o di fare snooze) utili ad esempio se ci si vuole riposare 40 minuti e poi essere svegliati

title: Non fa nulla in più rispetto a quanto offerto da iOS...
body:
Bella grafica, rapido e veloce l'inserimento dei promemoria, pero':

- non è integrata coi promemoria di iOS
- non si sincronizza con Google tasks
- non si possono associare differenti promemoria a differenti calendari
- i timer e la sveglia non aggiungono niente di nuovo rispetto a ciò che già è incluso in iOS, non si può prendere brani dalla libreria di iTunes, ad esempio.

+ possibilità di impostare la sincronizzazione automatica all'avvio
+ sincronizzazione e backup su DropBox
+/- sincronizzazione con iCloud, come documento, NON integrazione con Promemoria. In pratica, usa i 5GB free per salvare i propri dati e renderli disponibili sugli altri iDevices o sul Mac (se usasse Promemoria, sarebbero accessibili anche da Windows).

In conclusione: non aggiunge alcuna funzione di ciò che già si può fare con l'iOS di serie che la rendono  carissima per quello che è: un aggregatore, con una bella interfaccia, di funzioni di serie.

title: Good app gone bad
body:
Due was a very good app. Now, an update has come.

What a let-down!

I have NEVER before experienced that an update removes features from an app that you have to buy back if you want to keep using them.
Yet the developer is doing exactly that. Useful features such as pausing timers have disappeared and now you have to buy them back via an in-app update!
To me that looks like ripping off your loyal customers.

Apart from that, while it looks more polished, navigation is actually more complicated, defeating another great feature of the app as it was.

Due will be removed from my devices, and I will go looking for an alternative.

body: Det skal noe til å overgå denne! Den er kjapp, enkel og oversiktlig! Dette er en påminnelses app som varsler deg til eksempel 1. Lørdag i måneden, eller siste torsdag i måneden etc. for å huske trille opp søppel dunken for eks.! Jeg har lang erfaring med todo apps og har hatt de fleste. Denne står igjen sammen med iCal (kalender) og Things (huskelister). Genialt!:):) Den synker opp mot iCloud og funker perfekt mellom mine enheter (iPad/iPhone/iMac/MacBook Pro). Investering!😊

Dermed blir du minnet på gjøremålet etter hvert og det er lettere å få det gjort. Jeg legger også inn gjøremål som gjentas. F.eks. vaske badet, snu pulveraparatet, rense oppvaskmaskinen osv. Rutinemessig arbeid som jeg minnes på. Due kan lese vanlige setninger og gjøre det om til dato/klokkeslett. Dermed kan du ved hjelp av launchcenter eller drafts lett sende tekst til Due og vips så får du hjelp til å huske gjøremålet. Enkelt og greit.

title: Great, but...
body:
1. Could you introduce the “remind me on a location” feature that the regular Reminders has? This allows for consistency in variable schedules, for example; if a meeting takes longer than expected, then the usual reminders that starts of the evening routine will begin way too early, and it takes a lot of pushing around and extending to put it into order again. If those reminders just simply sat off as soon (or a set time period after) you arrived home, the entire experience would be a lot better and smoother.
2. Could you introduce “reminder chains” where a reminder sets off a set time period after a specified previous reminder is either set of, or preferably, marked done. This allows for small disturbances in a normal routine, for example a busy morning, without setting the whole morning out of it’s axis.

title: Very good reminder app
body: This app works great for reminders. I have been using it for about 2 years. Previously, I had various reminders in Apple's native calendar, clock and reminder apps plus a third party timer app but now, this app has taken the place of all 4 apps. I would still wish for 3 enhancements for this to be the perfect reminder app for me: 1) for me to use my own music or custom ringtones for the alerts as the alerts that come with the app are mostly too brief and don't attract one's attention; 2) to allow for reminders to be repeated during the space of 24 hours or less (to remind for things like medications every 6 hours, drink water every 2 hours from 11 am to 11 pm, etc); 3) to include a widget that can be added to the iPhone's Notifications screen. If these three enhancements can be made, this app would be perfect and I would definitely pay for the upgrade whereas the current enhancements for version 3 are frankly not attractive enough for me to do an upgrade. Thank you, developers, for coming up with this very useful app!

title: Incredibly intuitive and functional reminder and timer app
body:
This app continues to impress and I would still use the same three words - clean, smart, effective. (I have been using the app since its inception) Runs flawlessly on iOS8 and on my iPhone 6. Anyway, this is a spanking new and great update for users like me who continue to use it daily. 

I have tried organising my life with hardcopy organisers and setting calendar reminders but so far they are not as effective as Due. Due is great for a quick reminder to be set, yet has sufficient further features such as recurring reminders, address book integration, smart date/time recognition, sharing functions, etc that it can be as simple as you want, yet as functional if you desire.

As mentioned in my previous review some years back, it remains highly intuitive with the commonly used functions readily available such as quick setting of timings to 4 customisable favourite times and the quick way of snoozing different increments once the reminder kicks in. Everything feels right where they should be and the developer pays close attention to feedback and improves the app often. 

The reminder sounds available are plentiful and effective, and in fact with 2.0, we're too spoilt for choice! The app has come a long way and I have had no regrets using it for the past few years. Continue to surprise with more refinement and new features!

title: Reusable timers and alarms. Don't care for quality?—look elsewhere.
body:
Very well-designed, both functionally and aesthetically. Allows you to reuse and modify timers with ease, if, for example, you had to get up at different times every morning. The aptly-named egg timers are also useful, the skeuomorphic interface pleasing but not hindering.

The app design contains many subtle touches, such as the pinstriped background and the soft ticking when you start an egg timer; wonderful attention to detail has been paid.

All in all, an excellent app. The Dropbox functionality is useful for syncing timers across your iPhone and iPad. Those looking for a simple alarm app to wake them in the morning may well be justified in thinking that $4.99 is a little steep—that said, I don't regret purchasing this, so that's as good an indication as any.

title: This app is really top quality and probably the best of its kind
body:

If it allowed a back up that could be imported to restore all the reminders into the app rather than just a text file, and if it let you choose more friendly colors than black and white — like and earthtone green and/or other more pleasant colors. That said this app lets you set reminders and makes it as easy and seamless as possible— it also lets you add alarms to your reminders and the small price for it all is very much worth it, and they don’t charge you a subscription like some apps so you get what you pay for — you can get features after a year with a subscription which seems reasonable to help them develop for it, but it being unlocked once you buy it is important. There’s a lot of other details I haven’t mentioned here, but definitely just try the app out for a bit and see what you think of it

Edit: The developers responded to this post about how to back up data, which I appreciate — that said I would like to be able to back up my data locally to be restored later locally on my computer or elsewhere as I prefer to keep my data off the cloud. If this can be added it would be greatly appreciated and I would update this review

title: 11+ years with this app!
body:
I’ve been using this app for over eleven years now. Let that sink in. This app is so solid and reliable and user friendly that I have been using it consistently for that long. The absolute best and most important thing about it is that it is RELIABLE. Here’s the thing about reminder apps, or calendars, or whatever: they are only worth it if you can FULLY TRUST that once you put it in the app, it WILL remind you of it when you need it to. This app does that FLAWLESSLY, which is why it’s basically a necessity in my life lol. It’s like telling a close trusted friend “hey, can you call me on Tuesday to remind me I have to do that thing?” And knowing that you don’t have to spend the mental energy worrying about whether you’ll forget it because you know they’ll do it. That’s how this works. I put it in there, and I know, without a doubt, it will let me know what I needed to remember. In ELEVEN YEARS, it has NEVER ONCE failed me on this. Let that sink in too! Eleven years of reliability. Through grad school, early career, COVID times, pregnancy, parenting, law school, more new jobs, and even more. It’s universally helpful.

Part of this I think is because of the developer’s consistent and attentive updates. I’ve used this app through many generations of iPhone, and it’s always run smooth as butter. When there are bugs (which tbh I never even noticed), I see updates come swiftly. Also, the developer has consistently developed new features that integrate smoothly into the main function of the app and make the app easier to use. Some apps when they add new “features,” it kind of thins out the main feature of the app and becomes distracting. The new features have always just enhanced the core function of the app: to know, without a doubt, that if you put something in the app, it WILL remind you when you need it to (and will keep bugging you till you do the task if you want it to… this has been essential to me 😅)

Technically I have the main features of the app unlocked free because I initially purchased it before the subscription model started, but I still choose to pay for a subscription because it’s just that essential in my life.

In conclusion, this app is absolutely worth every penny and you should definitely download it if you are looking for a good reminder app. Thank you, developer!

title: Unusable with Apple Watch
body:
Love the app on the iPhone but incredibly annoying to use with Apple Watch. If you have stacked reminders (say 5 reminders at 9 AM), the expected behavior is for Apple Watch to buzz you once and say “5 notifications on Due.” It doesn’t. It buzzes you, 5 separate times. Even more annoying is that the app waits about 5-10 seconds between each buzz, so 5 notifications mean you get buzzed every 5-10 seconds for nearly a minute at every reminder or snooze period. I’ve contacted Due support who suggested some setting changes to minimize this behavior, but ultimately said, “it’s Apple’s system, we can’t do anything about it.” 

I had 14-25 notifications throughout the day. This means none stop buzzing all day. You can’t stop it either. You can’t push a button to stop. Even taking the watch off your wrist, it will continue through the notification cycle and you just have to wait if you don’t want to be buzzed constantly. 

Some days, it uses stacked notifications while other days, for no apparent reason, the app will bother you to death. 

If you’re an Apple Watch user, try a different app.

title: If I could give it 10 stars, I would
body:
I’ve had DUE for longer than I can remember, and I’ve always loved it. It’s simple, it’s easy, and—unlike so many other apps—it doesn’t cost a small fortune. It’s an affordable annual purchase (not an endless subscription), and it does exactly what it promises, in the cleanest and most straightforward way possible.
I never write app reviews because the best apps tend to fade into the background—you use them, rely on them, and stop thinking about them. But this app deserves recognition.
Earlier this year, I was diagnosed with ADHD, and everything suddenly clicked. I realized that DUE has always worked so well for me because of how frictionless it is. When something pops into my head that I need to remember, I can instantly throw it into DUE. No complexity. No setup. No mental overhead.
What truly sets this app apart is the reminder system. I don’t use calendars, task lists, or to‑do apps anymore because things get buried, endlessly snoozed, or turned into meaningless deadlines. DUE is different. If you don’t check something off, it just keeps reminding you—gently but persistently—without you having to manage or reset anything. That “nagging” feature works quietly in the background, doing exactly what it’s supposed to do. It’s simple, effective, and honestly kind of genius.
Now, DUE is where everything goes—anything I need to remember, no matter how big or small. And the funny thing is, I appreciate this app more now than I ever did when I downloaded it over five years ago. It continues to improve, continues to get better, and I genuinely don’t know what I would do without it.
Huge appreciation to the people behind this app for keeping it affordable, simple, and incredibly effective. This is the first app review I’ve ever submitted—and it’s long overdue.

title: Perfect balance between a reminder app and an alarm clock
body:
I’ve found Due to be the perfect balance between a reminder app and an alarm clock. By keeping only time-sensitive reminders, it ensures you’re not overloaded with notifications or becoming desensitized to them—something that can happen with other reminder apps. Due keeps you accountable without being overwhelming.

Beyond the app itself, the customer service is exceptional. I reached out three times with specific questions, and each time, I received thoughtful responses—either the same day or the next—along with personalized recommendations on how to make the most of the app. That level of support is rare and truly appreciated.

The only thing to be mindful of when importing reminders from Apple’s Reminders app is that Due automatically marks them as completed in the original app. However, there’s a simple workaround: instead of importing everything at once, you can hand-pick specific reminders to be imported without Due marking them as complete in iOS Reminders. To do this, turn on a setting named ‘Show in Side Menu’ under Due > Settings, in a section called System Reminders near the bottom. This lets you manually select reminders before they are added to Due.

I did a lot of research before choosing Due, and I’m happy to say it works well for me. But even if it hadn’t, I can see how it would still be a great fit for many people. It has plenty of features and customization options, making it versatile enough to suit different needs and workflows. If you’re looking for a powerful yet simple reminder system, Due is definitely worth considering. 

Overall, Due is a fantastic tool for anyone who wants an effective, no-fuss reminder system that actually helps you stay on top of tasks without bombarding you with notifications. Highly recommend!

title: It’s Good But Not Worth $8
body: Overall, the app is pretty good. It could definitely use an update to the UI to make it more modern looking. Not saying that it looks bad but compared with other applications in its price range, it’s quite lacking in UI. There are also some features that I think should be better. I think that setting up the alert should be more seamless for example, when you create a new task, you’re presented with a menu to name the task and put a date for the task to be completed. If you do not do it in a particular order and click the X button in the top right of the configuration box it will automatically place the alert on your task board. In my opinion There should be a large button that says done or something along those lines. This way, the user won’t be confused about clicking the X button and accidentally placing the task on their task board and having to go back and edit it later I can provide more examples if needed. I just think the UI could use a little bit of cleanup. There should also be a category directly on the left side of the screen with the other menu items that says completed alerts or completed tasks. I find it difficult to go back and view all of my completed tasks. I like how on the iPhones reminder system you can go view the grade out task that you have completed in the past. I still use the app every day. I think it could just use some fixes and UI cleanup for the eight dollar price tag that they’re charging realistically I’d say it’s more of a five dollar app.

title: No daily Repeat Feature? Don't Force Me to Edit Review
body: From Smartshoppennycounter I am a mature customer who can read well, comprehend, and follow a three-step process. I don't understand your directions on how to use this app. I am already giving up. I purchased this subscription a few hours ago, but I'm ready to cackle in the next few hours. I only need an app that shows the simplicity of setting up reminders to repeat daily. Leave alone the weekly repeat. I have spent hours looking for the clarity of the app’s daily repeat feature, and then I am triggered by irrelevant videos in the help section. How can weekly and monthly repeat features be open and accessible to the weekly and monthly repeat gesture but not for the daily feature? How can you only set the time for the day’s reminder but have not made it available or set it up to repeat? Which one comes first? The day of the week? Are you guys kidding with people's time and money? I don't want to watch irrelevant, waste-of-time videos to figure out solutions for what I have paid for. Please implore you to fix this problem, and that will convince me to embrace your persuasive advertisements about efficiency and customer-friendliness. Thanks. Smartshoppennycounter

title: Great tool for ADHD
body: This app is amazing! It helps me keep important tasks in view so I can check several times a day to see what I may have otherwise lost sight of. With Daily Recurring Tasks, I can check each task off for today, and it will pop up for me again tomorrow. NOTE: At first I had set each task with audible alarms and snooze timing, but soon learned that drove me crazy since I use Due for so many different tasks. Now, just the time-sensitive tasks are set that way and I set mundane tasks without alarms or snooze - that way they just pop up on a list of Due items and I can quickly mark several of them done throughout the day without as many nagging reminders. I also love being able to delay the timing for tasks if I’m running behind. If you’ll take the time to understand each of the features and options I think you’ll love this app, too!

title: Must set multiple reminders for same event
body: I just found out the app doesn’t support pre-alerts at given times. For example, if I have a concert to attend June 9 at 8pm, I would want to add that appointment a single time, and then be able to have reminders 1 week before, 2 days before, 1 day before, morning of and 2 hours before. Sounds like I would need to set 5 different reminders for that. Why not just have a single even with multiple reminders? I could set up a single reminder a week before, but then I would have to snooze if for 5 days, 1 day, 18 hours, 8 hours and 2 hours, which is way too much math. Also, it doesn’t let you snooze a certain number of minutes before the event, like 10 minutes before. Instead, you have to do math again to figure out the correct snooze interval so that it reminds you 10 mins before, and that interval might not be available. This is the problem with apps that make you pay before you can try them out.

body:

It’s also easy to say “I can’t do this for an hour” (or a day or whatever).

Sure, Apple has an app for reminders.  This is better and worth the money.

title: For super important tasks
body:
The only reminders app i can trust to handle  super important tasks.
They also are great at providing regular all maintenance; adding new clever features and updating bugs more than any other reminders app that I've used and embarrassingly I've tried them all 🫣. 

For me, Due is best used for my priority reminders and i use other apps for undated,  'later' or 'someday', 'projects' and other low urgency tasks.

It also works with Siri and has uncomplicated export options, which not all task apps are good at.

Highly recommend watching the less than five minute tutorial in the Help section , as I have been using the app for years, and still didn't realize some of the shortcuts the tutorial highlights.

The only two features I wish they have, is an editable notes entru field for individual reminders(like the Apple Reminders app has) and more help section screencasts. 

I thank 🙏the Due App team for creating an app I depend on to complete urgent time sensitive tasks thereby preventing me from f*ing up my life 🤪. 
P.S. the protaganist in the film 'Momento' should have definetly tried Due. 😂

title: This app would have received a 5-Star review if…
body:
UPDATE:
The developer responded to my complaint, and corrected the bug. I now have everything unlocked again! I updated my rating to 5 stars, because as I mentioned below, this is an incredible app!! Tons of thanks to the developer!!! 

They had been honest from the get go. Signing up you’re given the impression that whatever you have access to upon purchasing, you will maintain after the first year’s subscription(included in the initial purchase) is expired, EXCEPT for the new features. I’m here to tell you this is a lie. Just a moment ago, apparently one year later exactly TO THE MINUTE, I noticed my widget for this app no longer works, and I must pay the annual premium to be able to use its widgets. I now regret recommending this app to the dozens of people that I have, I feel as though I’ve misled them in some way. I see that the developer reads this stuff. This app has literally been a lifesaver, and I will continue to use it because it’s helped me manage my ADHD so well. But the lack of integrity and transparency upon the purchase is really disheartening. I’m still giving it 3 stars, as opposed to the 1 I almost gave it, because it truly is an incredible app, and has helped me have a more organized life.
