title: Recommended buy
body:
Like many others here, I'm using it daily. Until we have chip implants, I think this must be the most intuitive way to instantly turn a "gosh I have to..."-thought into a digital reminder. This app sets the benchmark for all other reminders, may it be as stand alone app or as feature inside another app (or site). 

The only thing I would change is the retro art deco striped background. (That's how hard it is to find anything critical to say about it) But actually I'm not looking at the app long enough during average usage to even notice it. (That's how fast it is.) 

Congratulation and thanks to the creators for a great app. 

*Gazing into the stars and thinking about future versions*..   like others, I use the timer function rarely. It's well done, but I keep forgetting that I have it. Strategically, functions like this might eventually find a more intuitive home either inside reminders (with a fifth "minute" dial?) or in separate little apps (or app shortcuts) sitting in separate "daily action" layers (or dimensions) of our future desktops. I'd like to see the space of the current timer button then be used for statistics, showing me what things I often need reminding for in my life and in what intervals etc. This app is so good, it would deserve this kind of back end expansion.

title: Perfect for the little things
body:
The latest update includes every feature I'd asked for in my last review, so 5 stars it is! :)

--------------------

Let me preface this by saying that Due is in no way a task manager - it's all about the little things. I use Things for my full-featured task manager.

Due is great for the stuff that falls through the cracks or clutters up a calendar/task manager - stuff like "rotate the laundry" or "mail mortgage payment," etc - things that need to get done at a specific time and are easy to check off or postpone for a few minutes right then and there. It uses local notifications and does a wonderful job of syncing between devices, and has a beautiful UI (although the tiny icons are unintuitive at first).

The one thing I would love to see is a more robust calendar scheduling system, with options like "Every First Monday" instead of just "Repeat every 15th". This would be much more helpful for some of the typical types of repeating tasks (like time sheets, dry cleaning, etc).

title: Pure elegance, flawless execution
body:
What could be a better mark of craftsmanship than shipping  an app that does something this "simple"—but which is designed and executed so thoughtfully that it can perform this supposedly simple thing in the most elegant, intelligent, and friction-free way imaginable. 

Due is there when you need it, it's blazingly fast to use, and then it gets and stays the heck out of your way. 

Like Instapaper, GoodReader, and Pastebot, Due is an essential piece of my iOS workflow that I can't imagine NOT using daily. And, I can highly recommend trying it for yourself. 

For every 500 iOS apps that the whackers slap together as a crashy and derivative $.99 "Hello World," there's maybe one or two as swell as Due. Maybe.

This is the sort of app that our friends at Apple should be putting in every demo to demonstrate the hard and careful work that the best iOS devs are shipping—apps that do all the heavy lifting to prove that iOS has the potential to become a truly first-class platform. 

If I could, I'd give Due 11 stars, a free steak dinner, and an embarrassingly sloppy French kiss. Bravo.

body:

It's so fast and simple to make a reminder, and I have several preset timers, like moving the laundry from the washer to the dryer that I use a lot.  This app is totally worth three bucks. I certainly recommend it.

New version: I do like the double tap to edit feature and the fact that you don't have to edit a reminder to change the snooze and alarm features. I would however like to see more options for snooze other than one minute or one hour. The fact that it's only those two options makes me hardly ever use the snooze feature. 
I would also recommend being able to sync with Mail and iCal's to do list so that I can see what I have to do on my computer and set reminders on my computer to later be used in Due. Overall though great update.

title: Good but could be improved
body:
I use Due on the iPad and iPhone.  I often check off an item on one device and a bit later get a reminder to do it on the other. I wish it had an option to sync periodically when the app is up instead of just on open and close. Perhaps it should try to sync before displaying a reminder?

It would be really nice if you had the option of snoozing directly from the reminder that pops up.  Now you have to view and then snooze the particular reminder.  

It is annoying that you have to set the time of the reminder first in some cases. If the time in the reminder is earlier than right now, it automatically rolls the date to tomorrow.  A brief delay in rolling this date would be handy.

I don't like that it reorders the list after each tap of snooze.  If I have another reminder that becomes due before the result of adding snooze to the current reminder, it reorders them and I end up tapping on the wrong reminder.  I would suggest putting in a delay of 3-5 seconds before reordering the list after snooze.  If I'm going to snooze multiple times, it should fall within that window.

I use Quick Access Timings all the time.  Very handy.

There is a bit of wasted space on the iPad version.  If I have reminders up, there is about 2" of space (vertically) that is unused on the left side of the panel.  I would suggest either having it fill the panel or putting the settings panel there when it is brought up.  Right now, settings is a floating panel.

Nice that it syncs with Dropbox.

Overall good and useful. Worth the $5 in my opinion.

The icons are cute but this app was supposed to cut the BS and get to the point. Not so here. Drop cute and don't make me think about interface. Also, three, the timer should start when I tell it to. Just because I prepared a timer does not mean I want it to start as soon as I am finished making it. It would be nice to have auto-start as an option, but not as your only choice. All in all, great app. I use it all the time.
Thank you.

title: Excellent, excellent app!
body:
This app does one thing, and one thing only: It bring a reliable recurring alarm to the iPhone. This is something that caused me a great deal of hesitation before I bought the iPhone (when my Treo finally died on me).  For all the wonderful features of the iPhone, having no recurring alarm that can be easily and quickly set makes it practically useless for me in many ways. So I had been searching every other day on the app store for an app like this one. Sure, it would have been nice if this simple function was an integral part of the iPhone OS (calendar or its native alarm), but since neither the iPhone calendar nor the native alarm has this function--an indispensable function for me, I am more than thrilled to have found this app. 

The recurring alarm keeps going off after a set interval--until you turn it off or reset the time. It has several quick-access buttons that allow you to delay the alarm for 10 minutes, an hour, or a day. Once the alarm is canceled, there is a "Logbook" where all the previous alarms are kept--which can be deleted if you so choose, but otherwise, the canceled ("Done") alarms are not visible.

title: Great app - excellent support
body:
I really like how quickly I can setup notifications - but even more importantly, the notifications will persist until I turn them off.  This is a huge piece of functionality that the native calendar app doesn't offer, and this app does it well. 

Only thing that would make this better is smaller increments of snooze times. 10 or 15 minutes would be perfect. The developer (who replied to my feedback extremely quickly and professionally) told me that this was due to limitations on apple's end though so doesn't look like there is much to do about it.

author: ScottMcGerik

title: Great App - More Sounds Please
body:
Update: I'm updating my review because as time goes on, I use this app more and more. It's so useful for a variety of reminders and timers. Really helps me stay organized and on top of the things. The only thing I ask for is more sounds!

The update definitely improves the functionality of this app by allowing shorter than 15 minute intervals. While I do find myself using this app on a daily basis, keep in mind that it's only good for setting quick reminders/alerts. If you want more structured or detailed reminders with a snooze option, stick to the calendar alerts in the native calendar app.

body:
I absolutely love this app!!!  Its easy to set up and no clutter.

But, I don't like the sounds I have to choose from; the long sounds are not very imaginative and the short sounds are much to short.  I don't want to hear another old fashioned phone ring, nor do I want a hurricane warning as the only sounds that last longer than 4 seconds.  
Please add more choices and the ability to change the length of each and every sound.

author: Bill favor

title: Already can't do without it.
body: There are certain situations where I want to be reminded of something, but don't want to clutter nor take the time to put it in my calendar. A phone call I need to make later today, a tv show I want to see tomorrow night, etc. It doesn't take the place of a full fledged task manager or a calendar. It's great at doing exactly what the app claims to do. It's a nice supplement to my workflow and fits a niche need quite well. Well worth the money for me.

title: Nice

author: rebrim

title: Excellent and quick
body:
Just yesterday I needed a quick reminder for an event a couple of hours away and I went into Calendar and it required a ton of steps to do it. With Due, it would have taken seconds.

I love the interface and that there's a difference between timers and reminders, especially the way it saves and lets you reuse them.

Perhaps it's a bit pricey for such a single-function app (though I feel silly complaining about something less than the price of a cup of coffee), and I would like it to add recurring reminders (e.g. weekly, bimonthly, etc), but definitely a useful, well-done app.
